headline: Google Cloud revenue spikes 82% thanks to AI adoption
summary: Alphabet's cloud business is booming, with revenue reaching $24.8 billion, driven by enterprise AI solutions and infrastructure. This growth significantly surpasses analyst expectations.
details: Alphabet investors have been concerned about the company's substantial AI spending, but Google's latest earnings report offers reassurance. The tech giant's cloud business, fueled by enterprise AI adoption, has seen remarkable growth.

Google Cloud revenue surged by 82% year-over-year, reaching $24.8 billion. This performance significantly outpaced the previous quarter's 63% growth and exceeded Wall Street's projected $22.46 billion.

The company attributed these cloud gains to the increasing adoption of enterprise AI solutions and infrastructure. Furthermore, Google Cloud's backlog of contracted work, yet to be converted into revenue, has climbed to an impressive $514 billion.

Alphabet's overall profit also saw a dramatic increase, hitting $112.1 billion compared to $28.1 billion in the same period last year. Total revenue grew 24% year-over-year to $119.8 billion, with Google Services revenue up 15% to $94.5 billion.

Google CEO Sundar Pichai expressed confidence, stating, "Our AI investments are redefining what’s possible across every part of our business." He highlighted strong momentum across the board, with Google's AI chatbot, Gemini, now boasting 950 million monthly active users.

Despite the strong performance, Alphabet's capital expenditures remain high, estimated between $180 billion and $190 billion for the year, covering data centers, chips, and infrastructure expansion. Pichai indicated that compute capacity investments are expected to pay off by 2027, citing strong demand and long-term deals as confidence boosters.
